scope.purpose: Machine-readable PRL physics decision tree from existing local eight-state KM and archived material responses.

notation.G: dC/dF at zero gate, or the declared symmetric finite-field secant; F definitions must not be pooled
notation.amplitude_control_sign: sign(C_l * G_l): positive strengthens |C_l| and negative weakens |C_l|, only when no endpoint sign crossing occurs
notation.rank_mismatch: A_C*A_G<0 after numerical sensitivity is applied

MoSSe_7269.status: full-shell tensor method accepted; archived 6x6 external-gate amplitudes remain exploratory rather than final mesh-converged constants
MoSSe_7269.mechanism_controls: Removing lower-valence/upper-empty mixing flips the representative lower C positive and transfers absolute gate dominance to the lower layer; isolated and smooth electrostatic references retain nearly equal layer slopes, unlike the full interface.

accepted_isolated_fact.relation: The lower and upper isolated structures are the same-oriented monolayer under a pure in-plane translation; +F maps to +F.
accepted_isolated_fact.implication: Both isolated building blocks have the same positive static response; their exact isolated static layer selectivity is zero by translation identity.

provisional_fixed_geometry_bilayer_obser.status: tensor/sign checks pass, but the geometry acceptance gate fails; this is not an accepted material result
provisional_fixed_geometry_bilayer_obser.force_pattern: At printed precision all in-plane forces vanish and the lower/upper layer-net z forces are +0.000174/-0.000174 eV/A, but the largest atomic force is -0.14124 eV/A on lower-layer S. The failure is dominated by internal vertical forces, not a rigid layer-translation force; it does not establish sliding or phonon stability.
provisional_fixed_geometry_bilayer_obser.interpretation_if_a_geometry_later_passe: A retained negative lower response would be an interface-induced reversal from two same-sign, translation-equivalent isolated layers.
provisional_fixed_geometry_bilayer_obser.gate_status: not submitted; G and the frozen gate-sensitive-layer prediction remain untested

MoSSe_7268.prediction_scoring: The frozen zero-gate signs and upper-static rank are provisionally observed across nb96/112, but the primary prediction cannot be scored because the geometry failed its force gate and no gate endpoints exist.

facts: The quadratic selected-channel criterion gives 0/8 correct full-endpoint layer gain directions for InSe under both internal-step and screened-external definitions.
The m001-related A and B domains have nearly the same negative net external-gate slope but opposite layer-contrast slopes and opposite amplitude-control directions.
For the largest windows, A has (G_lower,G_upper)=(+7.0866,-11.3107), while B has (-11.3514,+7.1195), in 1e-9 (V^2 T)^-1.
InSe_failure_boundary.rule: No criterion trained on MoSSe/MoS2 may be refit to force agreement with InSe; it must predict failure, abstention, or a separately measurable applicability condition.

prl_mainline.strongest_falsifiable_statement: An interface configuration can route the static response vector C and its external-field tangent G to different layers; the routing and the sign of amplitude control are separate observables conditioned by coherent interlayer response paths, not properties inferable from the net response or isolated-layer signs alone.
why_this_is_stronger_than_net_amplificat: MoSSe 7269 has only 2.2% retained static net response but 92.3% retained net gate slope, with static weight on the lower layer and gate susceptibility on the upper layer.

The provisional 7268 fixed geometry reverses the lower response from two identical positive isolated blocks, which is a sharper interface-rewriting signature than cancellation alone if it survives a geometry acceptance gate.
InSe A/B show that nearly identical net slopes can conceal opposite layer-control directions, making layer resolution experimentally discriminating rather than cosmetic.
causal_evidence_chain: Full-shell tensor/gauge validation establishes the response method for the 7269 anchor.
Matched isolated and smooth electrostatic references establish that ordinary layer Stark response is substantial but does not reproduce the full 7269 layer allocation.
Selected valence-conduction channel interventions causally change layer direction and gate allocation, conditional on frozen material subspaces.
The unchanged eight-state KM model supplies a held-out cross-path interference mechanism explaining why C direction and G control direction need not coincide.
InSe falsifies a universal low-order material criterion and defines the strong-mixing/screening boundary rather than being discarded.
not_claimed: registry-only control for the 7268/7269 pair, because termination, orientation, and registry co-vary
a direct laboratory knob that deletes or phase-flips one hopping channel
PRL novelty or experimental detectability already established

decision_tree.question: Does a declared 7268 fixed geometry satisfy the predeclared structural/response quality gates?
decision_tree.current_answer: no: max force 0.14124 eV/A exceeds 0.10 eV/A
decision_tree.pass_action: Only then accept the zero-gate C vector and consider independent +/-0.10 V/nm gate states.
decision_tree.fail_action: Do not submit gate states; retain the current C values only as a provisional fixed-geometry observation.
decision_tree.inconclusive_action: Resolve the geometry/protocol issue before any physics ranking claim.

decision_tree.requires: D0 pass on a future declared geometry
decision_tree.question: Do both translation-equivalent isolated layers remain same-sign while one accepted bilayer layer is resolved opposite?
decision_tree.pass_action: Call this interface-induced layer sign rewriting from identical isolated building blocks.
decision_tree.fail_action: Reject the identical-building-block sign-reversal claim; retain only the measured bilayer allocation.
decision_tree.inconclusive_action: No sign-rewrite claim if sign changes are comparable to window/mesh sensitivity.

decision_tree.question: Is A_C positive and A_G negative by more than declared numerical sensitivity, with no endpoint layer sign crossing?
decision_tree.pass_action: The frozen 7268 opposite-routing prediction passes; together with 7269 it gives a two-configuration swap of static and gate-dominant layers.
decision_tree.fail_action: The frozen prediction fails if either resolved rank has the opposite sign.
decision_tree.inconclusive_action: An unresolved rank is inconclusive only, never a failure or a pass.

decision_tree.requires: accepted full, isolated, and matched reference/control vectors under the same field definition
decision_tree.question: Can matched isolated or smooth electrostatic references reproduce the layer signs and normalized G allocation?
decision_tree.electrostatic_consistent: Reference and full vectors retain the same resolved component signs and gate-dominant layer, while a selected-channel intervention has no resolved effect beyond numerical-window variation.
decision_tree.coherent_path_supported: A reference fails a resolved sign/allocation feature and a fixed selected-channel intervention removes or reverses that same feature across retained windows.
decision_tree.mixed_or_unresolved: Classify as mixed/unresolved if only the net trend agrees, controls disagree with one another, or differences are cutoff-sensitive; no additive percentage is assigned.

decision_tree.question: Is there a resolved preregistered material contrast, a no-tuning same-orientation eight-state analogue, a retained InSe boundary, and a plausible two-weight layer readout?
decision_tree.pass_action: Advance the interface-conditioned C-versus-G routing mainline while separately auditing novelty and detectability.
decision_tree.fail_action: Keep the work as a mechanism/materials study; do not rescue it with a parameter scan, extra model states, or post-hoc material selection.

compatibility.implementation: AuditSpec(stacking='direct') sets both four-state diagonal blocks to the same complete monolayer Hamiltonian h; it requires no new orbitals.
compatibility.existing_direct_evidence: Stage-8 already evaluates the direct variant and finds a finite total Cxx, but it does not archive the layer-resolved C/G test needed for 7268.
compatibility.current_mapping_limit: All layer-resolved channel-control results in km-channel-control-20261110 use the default mirror stacking, where the isolated blocks have opposite Rashba structure and opposite response. They prove possible cross-path interference and C/G independence, but they are not a direct minimal model of 7268's identical positive isolated layers.

minimal_future_tests.gate: Run only if an accepted material geometry retains the same-sign-isolated-to-one-layer-reversed contrast.
minimal_future_tests.frozen_design: Use the existing eight-state parameters without fitting: direct stacking, fraction +/-0.25 partner registries, mass 45 meV, t=10 meV, U=0, and the established refined quadrature/probe settings. Evaluate t=0 isolated blocks and the full coupled layer C vector plus the symmetric internal-U slope G.
checks: The t=0 layer responses are identical and same-sign.
The +/-registry results satisfy the model's layer-exchange relation.
All sampled states remain insulating and layer sums close.
minimal_future_tests.pass: At a fixed registry the coupled model resolves one layer opposite to the identical isolated baseline, without parameter adjustment.
minimal_future_tests.fail: No resolved one-layer reversal; report that the present eight-state direct model does not capture the material contrast.
minimal_future_tests.stop_rule: Do not scan masses, hoppings, phases, or add states to obtain a pass.

minimal_future_tests.gate: Run only if KM_DIRECT_1 gives a resolved direct-stacking asymmetry or reversal.
minimal_future_tests.frozen_design: At the same one registry and parameters, compare full alpha=1 with removal alpha=0 of the already defined lower-valence/upper-empty channel; compute C and G only.
minimal_future_tests.pass: Removal abolishes/reverses the C or G allocation feature seen at alpha=1, supporting coherent path control within the model.
minimal_future_tests.fail: The feature survives the selected-channel removal; the chosen path is not its minimal cause.
minimal_future_tests.stop_rule: No alpha scan; existing mirror-stack phase tests already establish generic interference.

minimal_future_tests.gate: Only if KM_DIRECT_1 and KM_DIRECT_2 both pass and the material contrast is accepted.
minimal_future_tests.frozen_design: Use three nearby physical displacement points around the fixed direct registry to test whether A_G changes before a C sign changes.
minimal_future_tests.pass: Resolved re-routing of G with retained C signs supplies the minimal geometry-control analogue.
minimal_future_tests.fail: No resolved separation over the predeclared interval; stop rather than widen the scan.

pair: MoSSe BiDB 7268 same-orientation S/Se interface configuration
MoSSe BiDB 7269 mirror-related S/S interface configuration
primary_pair.reason: Same chemical bilayer family but different interface configuration, with sharply different isolated-layer parity: 7268 has two translation-equivalent positive isolated responses, whereas the established 7269 isolated reference is mirror-related with opposite static responses.
primary_pair.test: For each accepted geometry, compare full C/G with exact isolated-layer and matched smooth-electrostatic references, then apply the same frozen directional valence-conduction intervention. Judge component signs and normalized layer allocation, not pooled slope magnitudes across field definitions.
primary_pair.electrostatic_prediction: Matched references reproduce each configuration's resolved layer signs and dominant G layer; channel removal does not erase the contrast.
primary_pair.coherent_mixing_prediction: At least one full-interface sign/allocation differs from both references and is lost or reversed under the same fixed channel intervention.
primary_pair.current_limit: 7268 fails the force gate and has no gate endpoints, so the pair cannot yet decide the mechanism. The pair also co-varies termination, orientation, and registry, so any contrast is interface-conditioned rather than registry-only.

secondary_transfer_pair.role: Future isostructural transfer test only after the MoSSe decision tree is resolved and separately authorized.
secondary_transfer_pair.falsifier: Failure of the MoS2 layer-direction/gate-allocation pattern to transfer is compatible with vertex/coherent-mixing control and rejects a simple geometry-only rule; transfer alone would not prove electrostatics.
secondary_transfer_pair.status: not submitted; no WS2 response result exists

material_discrimination.mandatory_holdout: InSe 864 A/B remains the nontransfer/failure case for any low-order rule.

experimental_signature.principle: A net-only observable measures C_sum and G_sum; it cannot determine the layer contrast C_delta/G_delta or the two amplitude-control signs.
experimental_signature.minimum_readout: Use two independently calibrated layer-weight vectors, for example R1=C_lower+C_upper and R2=w_lower*C_lower+w_upper*C_upper with w_lower!=w_upper. The two-by-two weight matrix must be nonsingular; the same inversion applied to gate slopes reconstructs G.
experimental_signature.sharp_existing_example: InSe A and B have nearly equal negative G_sum (about -4.22 in the archived units) but opposite G_delta (about -18.40 versus +18.47) and opposite weakening/strengthening trends. A net-gate measurement alone would identify them as nearly the same response.
experimental_signature.MoSSe_signature: For 7269 the static net retains only 2.2% of the layer magnitudes while the gate slope retains 92.3%; a small zero-gate net signal followed by a large layer-weighted gate derivative is the expected cancellation-breaking signature.
experimental_signature.limitation: No specific contact, optical selection rule, signal-to-noise floor, orbital contribution, or device geometry has yet been validated.
